chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whichever believer proceeds with a believer regarding a dispute to a judge or a tyrannous ruler, so he judges against him with other than the judgment of God, then he has indeed become his partner in sin.

key_terms.حُكْم اللَّه: The judgment/law of God — divine rulings as transmitted through the Prophet and Imams
key_terms.سُلْطَان جَائِر: Tyrannous ruler — a ruler whose authority is not grounded in divine justice
key_terms.شَرِك فِي الْإِثْم: To be a partner in sin — complicity in wrongdoing through facilitating it
key_terms.قَاضٍ جَائِر: Unjust judge — a judge not operating by God's law as understood by the Imam

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about taking a fellow Muslim to an unjust judge or ruler?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that a believer who brings a fellow believer before an unjust judge or tyrannical ruler — resulting in a ruling contrary to God's law — bears shared moral responsibility for the sin. This ruling responds to the historical reality of Umayyad and early Abbasid courts where qadis (judges) often operated outside the bounds of Islamic jurisprudence as understood by the Imams. The original audience would have understood this as a warning that merely invoking an illegitimate judicial system against a fellow Muslim renders one a participant in the injustice that follows.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whichever Believer proceeds with a Believer regarding a dispute, to a judge or a tyrannous Sultan (ruling authority), so he judges against him with other than the Judgement of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he would be his partner in the sin’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Any believing person who takes another believing person before a judge or Sultan of injustice who then judges by means of something other than what Allah has sent, he becomes his (judge’s) partner in the sin.’”
